YOUR STOMACH CHANGES WITH AGE. YOUR HABITS SHOULD TOO.

Ever noticed how the same food that felt completely fine at 20 suddenly makes you feel heavy, bloated or gassy later in life?

Here’s what often happens 👇

👦 In childhood
Fast eating, fizzy drinks, constipation or certain food intolerances can trigger bloating and gas.

🧑 In your 20s–40s
Irregular meals, eating too fast, oily foods, low activity, stress and late-night eating can make digestion feel sluggish.

👴 After 50
Digestion and gut movement can become slower for some people, while constipation, food intolerance or certain medicines may contribute to bloating.

But here’s the good news:

Your daily habits can make a BIG difference.

🚶 MOVE
Take a 10–15 minute walk after meals. Gentle movement can support digestion.

🧘 TRY GENTLE YOGA
Pawanmuktasana, Vajrasana and gentle Cat-Cow movements may help with bloating and digestive comfort.

🥗 WATCH YOUR PLATE
Limit excessive fried/oily foods, carbonated drinks and foods that personally trigger your symptoms.

💧 HYDRATE SMART
Drink enough water throughout the day instead of waiting until you’re extremely thirsty.
And remember: you don't need to completely avoid water after eating—small amounts with meals are generally fine. There’s no strong evidence that drinking water after an oily meal “stops digestion.”

🕐 BUILD A ROUTINE
Eat slowly. Chew properly. Keep regular meal times. Stay active. Sleep well. Manage stress.

Because sometimes the solution isn't another medicine.

It’s a better routine.

«“A healthy stomach isn’t built in one day.
It’s built by the choices you repeat every day.”»

Eat smart. Move daily. Digest better. Live lighter.

You stand in the fiber aisle staring at two nearly identical tubs. One says Metamucil. One says Benefiber. They cost the same. They both promise regularity. But only ONE of them actually gels — and that changes literally everything. 🧪💩

Most articles say "they're basically the same, pick whichever." They're wrong.

💊 Are You Getting Enough Vitamins? 👀

Feeling tired all the time? Low energy? Frequent illnesses? Your body might be lacking essential vitamins.

✨ Here are 5 vitamins many people are commonly deficient in:

☀️ Vitamin D – Supports strong bones & immunity
🧠 Vitamin B12 – Keeps your brain, nerves & blood cells healthy
🌿 Vitamin B9 (Folate) – Essential for DNA synthesis & cell growth
🍊 Vitamin C – Boosts immunity & helps with wound healing
👁️ Vitamin A – Supports healthy vision & skin

⚠️ Don't self-diagnose! Symptoms alone can't confirm a vitamin deficiency. Always consult a healthcare professional before taking supplements.
